commit_repo_changes.description:
Stage only explicit files and create one Git commit; never push.

        The operation refuses pre-existing staged changes and directory paths so an MCP
        caller cannot accidentally sweep unrelated work into the commit. Git hooks are
        disabled by the host Repo Ops implementation for this deterministic path.

paths.description: Exact workdir-relative file paths to stage and commit
paths.title: Paths

commit_repo_changes.name: commit_repo_changes

create_directory.description:
Create ONE new directory. The parent must already exist.

        Not recursive: to create a/b/c, first create a/b, then a/b/c — each
        step is explicit and auditable. Fails with PATH_ALREADY_EXISTS if
        anything already occupies the path (an existing directory included),
        so a repeat call never performs a second change. Requires a
        read-write workdir.

path.description: Path of the directory to create, relative to the root
path.title: Path

create_directory.name: create_directory

create_text_file.description:
Create a NEW UTF-8 text file. Never overwrites an existing path.

        Use this only when the target does not exist — inspect it first with
        stat_file or list_directory if it might. If anything already occupies
        the path (file, directory or symlink) the call fails with
        PATH_ALREADY_EXISTS; there is no overwrite or force option. The
        parent directory must already exist. Content is written exactly as
        given (no newline or whitespace normalization) and published
        atomically, so a concurrent reader sees either no file or the whole
        file. Requires a read-write workdir.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content of the new file
content.title: Content

path.description: Path of the file to create, relative to the root
path.title: Path

create_text_file.name: create_text_file

delete_directory.description:
Permanently delete one EMPTY directory. Never recursive.

        Stat the directory first and pass its revision as expected_revision.
        If the directory holds anything at all — including hidden, denied or
        temporary entries — the call fails with DIRECTORY_NOT_EMPTY; list it
        and delete the contents first, one file at a time. There is no
        recursive or force option, and the deletion is permanent.

expected_revision.description: Revision returned by stat_file for this directory; the delete is refused if it changed since
expected_revision.title: Expected Revision

path.description: Path of the directory to delete, relative to the root
path.title: Path

delete_directory.name: delete_directory

delete_file.description:
Permanently delete one regular file.

        Stat or read it first and pass the current revision as
        expected_revision, so a file that changed (or was already replaced)
        is not deleted by mistake. Any regular file can be deleted, binary
        included — only *editing* is limited to UTF-8 text. Directories are
        not accepted here (see delete_directory) and symlinks are never
        followed or removed. The deletion is permanent: there is no trash,
        backup or undo.

expected_revision.description: Revision returned by stat_file or read_text_file for this file; the delete is refused if the file changed since
expected_revision.title: Expected Revision

path.description: Path of the file to delete, relative to the root
path.title: Path

delete_file.name: delete_file

download_binary_file.description:
Download one regular file through the optional raw-byte channel.

            The selected workdir must explicitly enable binary transfer. The
            file is read from one held descriptor, bounded by that workdir's
            binary transfer limit, and rejected if it changes while being
            read. The MCP result contains a standard binary resource block
            plus structured size/MIME/SHA-256/revision metadata.

path.description: File path relative to the workdir root
path.title: Path

download_binary_file.name: download_binary_file

outputSchema.description: Structured metadata returned alongside a binary MCP content block.

revision.title: Revision

sha256.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the raw bytes
sha256.title: Sha256

size.description: Exact number of raw bytes returned
size.title: Size

edit_text_file.description:
Replace exact text in an existing UTF-8 text file. Never creates one.

        Read the file first (read_text_file or stat_file) and pass the
        revision it returned as expected_revision; if the file has changed
        since, the call fails with REVISION_CONFLICT — re-read the file and
        retry with fresh text. If the path does not exist the call fails with
        PATH_NOT_FOUND: it will not create a file, so a mistyped path cannot
        silently become a new file.

        Each edit replaces every occurrence of exactly `old_text` and
        requires that count to equal `expected_count` (default 1); a mismatch
        fails with EDIT_CONFLICT, so include enough surrounding context to
        make the match unique. All edits in one call are applied in order and
        are all-or-nothing: if one fails, the file is left untouched.
        Deletions and replacements happen in a single atomic step, so no
        reader ever sees a partial file.

expected_count.description: Number of occurrences old_text must have; else EDIT_CONFLICT
expected_count.title: Expected Count

old_text.description: Exact text to replace. Empty is allowed only to fill a completely empty file. Include enough context to make the match unique.
old_text.title: Old Text

edits.description: Exact-match text edits, applied in order
edits.title: Edits

expected_revision.description: Revision returned by read_text_file or stat_file for this file; the edit is refused if the file changed since
expected_revision.title: Expected Revision

path.description: Path of the file to edit, relative to the root
path.title: Path

edit_text_file.name: edit_text_file

revision.description: Revision of the file after the edit
revision.title: Revision

        This never starts an Agent runtime. `status` and `actions` accept no paths;
        `diff` and `staged_diff` require explicit policy-valid paths. Status path lists
        are filtered through the ServerFS path/deny policy before they are returned.
        Output is bounded by the host Repo Ops service.

run_repo_action.description:
Run one fixed administrator-configured repository action.

        The executable and base argv are not request parameters. No shell is used. Named
        actions require a read-write workdir and always take the host writer lease, including
        logically read-only checks, so integrity verification cannot race ServerFS/Agent writes.
        A path is accepted only when that action declares a path argument and must pass the
        same ServerFS path policy as filesystem tools. Built-in release actions instead
        accept only release_tag, validate semver, and fix HEAD/repository/workflow internally.
        Unknown parameters such as force, commit, remote or workflow are rejected.

path.description: Optional workdir-relative path accepted only by path actions
path.title: Path

release_tag.description: Release action only: vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH or vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-beta.N
release_tag.title: Release Tag

run_repo_action.name: run_repo_action

        result limit is global: the search stops as soon as enough

path.title: Path

send_agent_message.description:
Steer an active task with a narrow follow-up when live_steer is supported.

        Keep steering within the task's existing authorized objective and mutation scope.
        If the requested work is a distinct objective, submit a new atomic task instead.
        For a terminal task, submit a new atomic task. Use continue_from_task_id only on
        supported v1 endpoints, never on signed-v2 Core endpoints. Runtimes such as
        Claude or Qoder may reject live steering even while active.

message.description: Narrow follow-up for the active task; include only information required to steer the current objective without expanding its authorized scope
message.title: Message

send_agent_message.name: send_agent_message

Get metadata for one file or directory.

        Returns type (file/directory/symlink/other), size, modified time
        (RFC 3339 UTC) and best-effort MIME type. A symlink as the FINAL
        component is reported as type "symlink" (target never revealed);
        symlinks in parent components are rejected.

path.title: Path

modified_at.description: Last modification time as RFC 3339 UTC
modified_at.title: Modified At

revision.title: Revision

size.title: Size

submit_agent_task.description:
Submit one narrow authorized Agent objective and return a task handle.

        Keep the task atomic: provide only the context required for the objective,
        explicitly bound allowed mutations and stop conditions, and prefer existing
        structured project workflows over embedding unrelated shell/network/security
        implementation detail. This guidance reduces ambiguity and accidental scope
        expansion; it does not weaken or bypass provider safety checks.

        The call never waits for provider completion. Poll get_agent_task or
        read_agent_task_events. On signed-v2 Core endpoints, omit continue_from_task_id
        and idempotency_key. Use list_agent_tasks on the authorized workdir to rediscover
        an existing task after an uncertain submission or client restart. Submit a new
        atomic task for distinct work; native session continuation is available only on
        supported v1 endpoints.

continue_from_task_id.description: Prior terminal ServerFS Agent task to resume, only on supported v1 endpoints. Omit on signed-v2 Core endpoints; continuation is not supported.
continue_from_task_id.title: Continue From Task Id

correlation_id.description: Optional opaque correlation identifier (UTF-8, at most 256 bytes); stored as metadata only and never forwarded as provider instructions
correlation_id.title: Correlation Id

idempotency_key.description: Optional retry key for one logical submission on supported v1 endpoints. Omit on signed-v2 Core endpoints; discover tasks rather than retry blindly.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

model.description: Optional provider-native model identifier for this task only. Omit it to preserve the runtime's native default or resumed-session model.
model.title: Model

path.description: Relative starting directory inside the workdir
path.title: Path

profile.description: Provider-neutral execution profile; native Codex/Claude/Qoder require workspace-write
profile.title: Profile

prompt.description: One narrow authorized objective for the delegated Agent. Include only the context needed to complete that objective, state the allowed mutation scope and stop conditions, and prefer structured project actions over unrelated implementation detail.
prompt.title: Prompt

runtime.description: Configured Agent runtime: codex, claude, qoder, or configured acp-<profile-id>

upload_binary_file.description:
Create or revision-guardedly replace one regular file from raw bytes.

            Binary transfer must be enabled for the selected read-write
            workdir. overwrite=false is create-only and never replaces an
            existing path. overwrite=true requires expected_revision and
            atomically replaces exactly the regular file at that revision,
            preserving metadata and rejecting multiple hard links.

download_url.title: Download Url

OpenAIFileInput.title: OpenAIFileInput

data_base64.title: Data Base64

expected_revision.description: Required only when overwrite=true; current revision from stat_file or download_binary_file
expected_revision.title: Expected Revision

file.description: Optional ChatGPT/OpenAI file parameter; provide exactly one of data_base64 or file

overwrite.description: False creates a new file; true replaces one existing regular file and requires expected_revision
overwrite.title: Overwrite

path.description: Path of the new file, relative to the workdir root
path.title: Path

upload_binary_file.name: upload_binary_file

revision_before.title: Revision Before
